standard.title: Safely make designed solutions
standard.description: use materials, components, tools, equipment and techniques to safely make designed solutions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use materials and equipment to make solutions safely (AC9TDEFP01). They have practised basic joining and construction techniques. They have not yet deliberately selected materials for a purpose, or demonstrated safe use of a range of tools and techniques across different construction contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use materials, components, tools, equipment and techniques to safely make designed solutions across different construction contexts.

nodes.label: Selecting and using materials for a purpose
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify appropriate materials for a designed solution and explain why they are suitable
nodes.minimum_width: Select at least one material for a construction task and state one reason why it is appropriate for the purpose
nodes.typical_width: Select materials, components and joining materials appropriate for the design; explain why each material suits the purpose; consider re-use of available materials where appropriate
wider: Explore how available materials can be re-used — for example using wrapping paper and gift cards to make classroom decorations; explain how re-use minimises waste
Select materials to show how properties are appropriate for particular designed solutions — materials that enable sliding, floating or flying

response_modes.reason: Material selection requires students to reason from purpose to property — 'I need it to float, so I need a material that is light and waterproof'. Without this scaffold, students select materials by preference or availability rather than suitability. A reasoning sequence (what does it need to do? what material property is needed? which materials have that property?) builds deliberate selection.

success_criteria: Names at least one material selected for the task
Gives at least one reason why that material is appropriate for the purpose
nodes.hinge_reason: Material selection reasoning feeds directly into Node 2's safe making — students who select materials by preference rather than suitability are likely to attempt construction with inappropriate materials, creating safety risks and non-functional outcomes.

nodes.label: Using tools and techniques safely
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can practise a range of technical skills using tools and equipment safely
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two tools or techniques safely in a construction context (e.g. cutting, joining, measuring, planting, preparing food with a knife)
nodes.typical_width: Practise a range of technical skills across different construction contexts — joining techniques, watering and mulching gardens, preparing a recipe using a knife safely; follow safety expectations consistently
wider: Assemble components for a musical shaker (container, contents, joining materials) — check they function as planned after assembly; explain the joining technique used and why it was chosen
Use joining techniques when making a product from multiple materials — identify which joining technique is appropriate for each material pair and explain why

response_modes.reason: Safe tool use is a procedural skill requiring consistent, repeated practice across different tools and materials. Each tool or technique has its own safety requirements and physical demands. Consolidation here is the primary response — accuracy, consistency and safety develop through practice, not through encountering more contexts.

success_criteria: Uses at least two tools or techniques correctly and safely
Follows safety expectations for each tool — no unsafe actions observed
